black.tagline: Last to arrive. First to apologize. Never on time.
knownFor: Being the last team to submit a name (PNN-001).
Bribing the witches before the witches had opened for business (PNN-002).
Being webbed by the Pyro Posse, then announced last (PNN-005).
A team name that is three words and a second B.
black.file:
The **Black Webb Bandits** chose spiders, a creature famous for patience, planning, and sitting very still until something happens to it. They then embodied the theme perfectly. The first entry in the file is the name reveal: last in the neighborhood, with a pun so tightly packed that PNN suspects it took a full week to find the second B.

The second entry is the bribe. Having failed to be first, the Bandits went for early. They arrived with treats and a flier asking 'Are you a witch?' before the witches had announced the instructions. The witches said NO. The Bandits are the only team in the game to have visited a starting line and somehow finished behind it.

The third entry is the Pyro Posse's visit, which wrapped a For Sale sign in orange cobweb and left a field of orange flags in the grass. The Bandits were pranked, and then, adding insult to webbing, announced last. A spider caught in someone else's web is a headline PNN has now written twice.

In fairness, the Bandits have charm, a genuinely great logo, and a name that makes people say 'oh, I get it.' Those are real assets. Clueso notes that none of them are punctuality.
strengths: Excellent logo. Eight legs, no regrets.
A flair for dramatic entrances, when they arrive.
weaknesses: Starting lines, finish lines, and every line in between.
black.advice: Set an alarm. Then set a second alarm to remind you about the first alarm. Then arrive on time, which is the one prank nobody will see coming.

green.tagline: The truth is out there. So is the trash.
knownFor: Being outed by its own recycling (PNN-004).
A team name that promises secrets and a trash can that kept none.
Declining to comment, loudly.
Agents, a saucer, and a cow with a complaint.
green.file:
The **Area 51 Bureau** built its brand on secrecy: agents, a flying saucer, a cow in mid-abduction. A team like that is supposed to be impossible to catch. Then the Pyro Posse crowned two garbage cans with balloons and tissue-paper flames, and the Bureau's cover-up was blown by its own driveway.

PNN reminds the Bureau that Roswell was a long time ago and this was in front of the house. The cans were not abducted. They were accessorized. For a team that exists to bury the truth, there are now several balloons on it.

The Bureau has declined to comment. PNN considers this consistent with the file, which the Bureau has redacted several times on its own, to be safe. The redactions are the most informative part.

In fairness, the poster the Posse made of the Bureau looks like a movie, and 'A Dumpster Fire. Disaster.' is a title most teams would trade a witch for. The Bureau's only real vulnerability is the one thing it cannot classify: the curb.
strengths: A genuinely good logo, with agents.
Total commitment to the bit. The bit is secrecy.
weaknesses: Anything visible from space, including balloons.
green.advice: Bring the bins in. Then deny you ever had bins.

knownFor: A fire theme delivered, in PNN-004, with balloons.
Three pranks in one night, plus a fourth they forgot to mention (PNN-005).
Posting the photos before the victims got home, then deleting them.
Telling the game group 'It's like we're the only ones playing.'
orange.file:
The **Pyro Posse** arrived with the boldest brand in the game: fire, a promise to 'bring them to ash,' and poster art that looks like it has its own budget. Then they went to the party store. In PNN-004 the flames were balloons and tissue paper. PNN admires the confidence. PNN also admires the receipt.

By PNN-005 the Posse had escalated to actual laundry, actual smoke, and a poem narrated by underwear. They pranked the Tightie Whities, the Silver Bullets, and the Black Webb Bandits in a single night. That is a lot of work. It is also a lot of photos, which the Posse posted to the game group before the victims got home, spoiling the surprise for exactly the people it was built for.

> Sometimes I am fast…. Usually when I shouldn’t be.
> — a Pyro Posse member, on the deleted photos

The Posse also declared, 'It’s like we’re the only ones playing,' which is what a runner says after the first mile of a marathon. They then forgot to mention one of their own pranks for a day. They have pranked four teams and can count three.

For the record, PNN reminds the Posse that actual fire is not part of the game. A paper flame on a stick delivers all the drama and none of the paperwork. The Posse owns a great many paper flames. This is fine.
strengths: Poster art that could frighten a lesser team.
A work rate that makes everyone else look like tourists.
weaknesses: The delete button, which they find too late.
orange.advice: Wait until the victim has seen the prank before you post it. It will be the best surprise you ever delivered.

pink.threatLevel: Unknown. Clueso refuses to rate himself.
knownFor: Being the team Inspector Clueso is certain is guilty.
Not appearing in a single case file. Clueso finds this suspicious.
Running a whole newsroom, hotline, newsletter, and Corrections Desk.
Guilty until proven guilty.
pink.file:
The **Prowling Purrpetrators** are the only team in the neighborhood Inspector Clueso has never caught. He has been trying for five cases. The file contains: nothing. The file is very thick. Clueso says the thickness is the point.

The pink team operates a full newsroom, a hotline, a newsletter, and a Corrections Desk. Clueso has noted that a team this busy is either extremely innocent or extremely guilty, and he has chosen 'extremely guilty' because 'extremely innocent' does not make a good headline.

No pink prank has been reported, photographed, posted, or deleted. Clueso believes this is a masterclass in not being caught. Everyone else believes it is a masterclass in not doing anything. The truth is probably somewhere between. Clueso will not be taking questions.

The Purrpetrators decline to confirm or deny. They are, as always, wearing sunglasses.
strengths: A newsroom, a hotline, and a newsletter, all on one team.
weaknesses: Every other team has a case file. They have a feeling.
pink.advice: Prank someone. Anyone. Clueso is begging. He would like to be right.

red.threatLevel: Unknown. Clueso has not met them.
knownFor: Not appearing in a single case file.
A name that sounds like a very serious rap group.
Being the quietest team in the game, which is suspicious.
Existing. Allegedly.
red.file:
**The Crimson Crew** is the only team that has not yet appeared in a PNN case file as a subject, a victim, a suspect, or a punchline. Clueso finds this slightly insulting. He has been circling the team's name on the list with a red pen.

Possible explanations: they are planning something enormous. They are planning something small. They are planning nothing. They are lost. Clueso favors 'planning something enormous' because 'lost' is the Black Webb Bandits' department.

PNN has no complaints about the Crimson Crew. This is the complaint. A team with a name like that should be setting something off, hoisting something up, or at least hanging something from a flagpole. PNN has checked the flagpoles. Nobody is hoisting.

In fairness, a quiet team is a dangerous team, which Clueso says about every team, including this one. The Crew may be waiting for the right moment. The right moment is now. The party is October 24.
strengths: A sharp, serious name. Nobody is laughing at the name.
A clean record, which has made PNN nervous.
red.advice: Do something, anything, loudly and within the rules. Clueso has an empty folder labeled 'Crimson' and he is tired of looking at it.

silver.tagline: The only bullet that needs directions.
knownFor: A clothesline of unidentified laundry hung at their home during the football game (PNN-005).
A poster calling them 'Slow, Unsure, and Completely Disoriented.'
A flagpole that was never asked to do anything.
A name that suggests werewolf-slayers and a record that suggests laundry.
silver.file:
The **Silver Bullets** chose a name meant to be fast, shiny, and fatal to monsters. PNN has yet to see any of the three. In PNN-005 the Pyro Posse hung a clothesline of charred, unidentified laundry on their lawn while they were away at football games, and the Bullets, to their credit, have still not identified it. Nobody has. The laundry has issued no statement. Neither has the Posse.

The poster at the Bullets' door read 'Slow, Unsure, and Completely Disoriented.' A bullet that is slow, unsure, and disoriented is, ballistically, a pebble. This is not an insult. It is physics.

The Silver Bullets also own a flagpole. As far as PNN can tell, it has been used for nothing. A flagpole is the one structure on Earth built to hoist things where the whole neighborhood can salute them. The Posse hung the laundry low instead, which the flagpole took personally.

In fairness, being pranked while you are out at a game is the best possible reason to be disoriented. The Bullets were at the stadium and got blitzed at home. That is not slow. That is football.
strengths: An alibi so airtight it was literally a football game.
weaknesses: Knowing what is on their own clothesline.
silver.advice: Hoist something. Anything. The flagpole has been waiting a very long time.

knownFor: Two dogs, two walks, and a very awkward 'how long have you had it?' (PNN-003).
Being the target of the most obvious prank in the history of obvious pranks (PNN-005).
Having a pair of scorched satin bloomers named in their honor.
A team name that practically volunteers.
white.file:
The **Tightie Whities** named their team after underwear and then, remarkably, acted surprised. Anyone who names a team that way has pre-approved the joke. The Pyro Posse took the invitation literally and hung a clothesline of laundry on their walk. Then they lit it.

The garment in question was a pair of white satin bloomers. They are not tight. After treatment, they are not white. The charring ran down the middle in a pattern a banner on the same line called 'The Skidmark Synod.' PNN did not name it. PNN would have fought for the word 'Synod' to be somewhere else.

Earlier, in PNN-003, the Whities were spotted walking dogs downhill a few minutes apart. When a neighbor asked how long one member had owned a dog, the answer was a pause. PNN has not recovered from the pause. Clueso filed it as *Operation Loose End* and has refused to elaborate.

The team has a tight name, a loose story, and a gift for being the one everyone notices. In fairness, that is the right gift for a team named after underwear: you cannot go unnoticed. You can only be uncovered.
weaknesses: The word 'loose,' which has followed them everywhere.
white.advice: Rehearse saying 'about two years.' Then buy a lock for the clothesline.
